subject: MSA + Order Form: output use, training carveouts, and feedback license
messages:
From: Danielle Price <d.price@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Berger <t.berger@procure.nimbushealth.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 15:03:00 -0500
Subject: Nimbus MSA + Order Form (redlines attached)

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for the draft MSA and Order Form. Our procurement & legal teams have gone through both and attached a redline set (Nimbus_MSA_redlines_v2.docx) plus an annotated Order Form PDF. High-level items they care most about:

- Output ownership: they want explicit confirmation that Nimbus retains ownership of outputs generated from their prompts and data.
- Training / model use: clause clarity that Redwood will not use Nimbus data or outputs to further train or improve model weights without explicit written opt-in.
- Feedback license: they are worried about a broad feedback/telemetry license that could be used to monetize or retrain models. They are open to telemetry for service improvement but want strong de-identification and no model-training rights.

Can you loop in Redwood legal and propose language we can review? We prefer tracked changes in the MSA so our GC can sign off.

Attached: Nimbus_MSA_redlines_v2.docx, OrderForm_NIM_20261110.pdf

Proposed next step: 30-min call early next week to align. Are you available Wed 11/17 or Thu 11/18?

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Price
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Nimbus MSA + Order Form (redlines attached)

Danielle — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Looping in our legal lead (Laura) and sales engineer (Marissa) so we can surface any technical constraints. Quick responses to the three bullets above:

- Output ownership: we generally accept customer ownership of customer-provided data and outputs. We'll propose specific wording that preserves Redwood's right to derive aggregated metrics (non-identifying) for monitoring/SLAs.
- Training / model use: we need to confirm whether "no training" is a hard prohibition or whether a de-identified, aggregate-only opt-in is acceptable. Laura, can you propose a clause that gives Nimbus a strict opt-out but allows for an explicit opt-in path?
- Feedback license: we can propose a narrow feedback license limited to aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement and debugging, not for training new models or selling derivative models.

We're available for a 30-min sync on Thu 11/18 at 10am ET — Marissa, please hold that. Danielle, if that doesn't work, suggest an alternative.

I'll produce a short summary of proposed clause language from Legal and share a tracked-change MSA by EOD Friday.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:34:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nimbus redlines - proposed positions

Team — reviewed Nimbus's redlines and marked up an internal proposal. Key points and recommended language (high level):

1) Output ownership
- Recommend: Customer retains ownership of Customer Data and Customer Outputs. Add clarification that "Customer Outputs" means content generated solely in response to Customer-provided prompts/data. Redwood may retain aggregated, de-identified usage metrics for operational purposes and to meet SLA obligations but may not assert ownership over Customer Outputs.

2) Training / Model use
- Recommend a two-track approach:
  a) Default: Redwood will NOT use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train or improve model weights or for model re-training.
  b) Optional opt-in: Customer may separately agree to a Training Addendum that grants a time-limited, revocable license for de-identified data to be used for research/improvement; this must be explicit and compensated.

3) Feedback license
- Recommend limiting any feedback/telemetry license to: aggregate, de-identified telemetry and error traces strictly for service reliability and product improvement. Carve out: no rights to use that data to train production models or for commercial model derivation.

Open questions / asks for Sales:
- Is there any Nimbus technical constraint that requires different language around "de-identification"? Marissa / Karthik pls confirm.
- Would Sales accept an "opt-in paid training" path for larger customers (we should use a templated Training Addendum)?

Attachments: proposed_clause_suggestions.docx (I'll prepare tracked-change language once we align). I'd like Sergio to send the high-level summary + proposed wording to Danielle so their GC sees we're narrowing the ask.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Price <d.price@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Nimbus Health Legal <legal@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -0500
Subject: Proposed positions on Output & Training clauses (follow-up)

Danielle — attaching a short summary and next steps. Per legal, here's the proposed compromise language we can include in the MSA (high-level, will send tracked changes soon):

- Customer Outputs: "Customer retains sole and exclusive ownership of Customer Outputs. 'Customer Outputs' means content generated by the Services in response to Customer-provided prompts or inputs during Customer's use of the Services. Redwood may collect and retain aggregated, de-identified usage metrics solely for operational purposes and to monitor SLAs, but shall not assert ownership of Customer Outputs nor use Customer Outputs to create or improve model weights unless Customer provides an explicit, written opt-in."

- Training: "Except as expressly set forth in a separate Training Addendum executed by the parties, Redwood will not use Customer Data or Customer Outputs to train, tune, or improve model weights or models used for production services. A Training Addendum, if executed, will be limited in scope, timebound, revocable, and subject to a commercial arrangement."

- Feedback license: "Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide license to use aggregated and de-identified telemetry and feedback for the sole purpose of service reliability, debugging, and product improvement. Such data will not be used to train production model weights or to create productized models for sale to third parties."

We also put together a tracked MSA with those clauses highlighted (will upload to the Google Doc linked here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-proposed-output-clauses) and opened a DocuSign envelope for the current Order Form (link below).

DocuSign (Order Form): https://docusign.com/signon?token=ABC123-nimbus-order
Shared doc with proposed clauses: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-proposed-output-clauses

If these principles look acceptable to Nimbus, Laura will incorporate them into a tracked-change MSA and we can route that for signature. If Nimbus needs stronger wording (e.g., absolute ban on any derivative research use), please flag specifics so Laura can address them.

Available for a call Thu 11/18 10am ET as proposed.

Best,
Sergio

From: Danielle Price <d.price@nimbushealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Berger <t.berger@procure.nimbushealth.com>, Nimbus Health Legal <legal@nimbushealth.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: output use, training carveouts, and feedback license

Sergio / Laura — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed language. High-level response from our GC:

- Output ownership language looks good in principle; they'd like a sentence that explicitly states "Customer Outputs will not be used by Redwood for model training or model improvement absent Customer's prior written consent." (Your draft already says similar, but they want the explicit "will not be used" phrasing.)
- Training Addendum approach is acceptable; they want clarity on the revocation process (how quickly opt-in can be revoked and consequences). Can you add a clause that the opt-in is revocable with 30 days notice and that no further training will occur on newly designated data after revocation?
- Feedback license: they want stronger assurance that de-identification standards align with NIST SP 800-188 (they referenced an internal policy).

Request: Could you share a tracked-change MSA with your final suggested wording by EOD Mon 11/22? Our team wants to review before the 11/22 call. If possible, add the revocation language and the explicit "will not be used" sentence.

We'll confirm call attendance after our GC reviews the tracked MSA.

Thanks,
Danielle
Danielle Price
Head of Procurement, Nimbus Health
